Mod tools are a core necessity of Voat that Reddit has ignored on its own site for a long time. Providing better mod tools would strengthen Voat because of how much work the mods do collectively to help users, answer questions, and respond to spam. Mod mail is the heart of a moderator's tool box, so what if Voat implemented mod mail like an IT trouble ticket system? I know this would take a while to implement, but Voat could include common ticketing system features like:

  • Trouble ticket filtering/sorting and moving tickets into folders
  • Assigning tickets to different mods manually or based on type
  • categorize trouble tickets with tags
  • Saved replies (canned responses) that could be saved and inserted into common tickets
  • Collision detection for when two mods are replying to the same ticket (maybe a "mod1 is typing" message)
  • a search system so that you can find previous responses to similar tickets
  • have the system show internally which mods are online so that you know when you're the only one available to respond to tickets

These are just suggestions, but I think that the task and response nature of spam and user help requests lends itself well to a ticketing system, and it might be a good way to improve upon the mod tools that were available at Reddit.
What if Voat made mod mail like a trouble ticketing system?

This might only be feasible in the long-term, but a trouble ticket system has more powerful problem resolution tools than a mailbox, and where mail is useful for communication, the task driven nature of moderating might lend itself better to a trouble ticket system.
